title: Successive run decomposition
statement: Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program over them, and let $x$ be a bit string. For every abstract state $s$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the state reached after $t+1$ steps from $s$ equals the state reached after $t$ steps from the state obtained by one step of $P$ on $x$ from $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A counter program $P$ over these registers and labels
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, $x$ an input bit
string, $s$ an abstract state and $t \in \mathbb{N}$. Running $t + 1$ steps from $s$ equals
running $t$ steps from the state obtained by one step of $P$ on $x$ from $s$:
$\mathrm{run}_{P,x}(s, t + 1) = \mathrm{run}_{P,x}(\mathrm{step}_{P,x}(s), t)$.
